description: The reference-culture GAMING world: video games as an art form and the specific referents the reference faculty needs (BioShock, Portal). A modern-region anchor.

microtheory.name: video_games
microtheory.definition: Video games as a cultural / interactive art form (post-1958): a player acts on a simulated world through a controller, progresses through levels, and the medium has its own canon of referents (BioShock, Portal, Half-Life). The modern world Cornelius Vane, a Victorian of 1885, has no concept of.

concepts.name: game
concepts.definition: An interactive rule-governed system a player engages for play, challenge or story.

concepts.name: player
concepts.definition: The human agent who acts within a game world through its controls.

concepts.name: controller
concepts.definition: The input device (gamepad, keyboard) through which the player acts on the game.

concepts.name: console
concepts.definition: A dedicated gaming computer (Xbox, PlayStation, Nintendo) that runs games.

concepts.name: level
concepts.definition: A discrete bounded stage or map the player traverses within a game.

concepts.name: respawn
concepts.definition: Re-instantiation of the player's avatar after death, at a checkpoint.

concepts.name: checkpoint
concepts.definition: A saved position a game returns the player to on failure.

concepts.name: boss
concepts.definition: A large, distinct enemy gating progress, usually ending a level.

concepts.name: quest
concepts.definition: A structured objective or mission the player undertakes in a game.

concepts.name: npc
concepts.definition: A non-player character controlled by the game rather than the player.

concepts.name: cutscene
concepts.definition: A non-interactive cinematic sequence that advances a game's story.

concepts.name: gameplay
concepts.definition: The interactive mechanics and player experience a game affords.

concepts.name: bioshock
concepts.definition: A 2007 first-person game (Irrational Games) set in the underwater city Rapture; source of the mind-control trigger phrase 'would you kindly'.

concepts.name: rapture
concepts.definition: The undersea objectivist dystopia that is the setting of BioShock.

concepts.name: andrew_ryan
concepts.definition: Rapture's founder, an objectivist industrialist; BioShock's tragic antagonist.

concepts.name: splicer
concepts.definition: A gene-spliced, ADAM-addicted inhabitant of BioShock's Rapture.

concepts.name: plasmid
concepts.definition: A genetic tonic granting powers in BioShock.

concepts.name: big_daddy
concepts.definition: An armoured protector of a Little Sister in BioShock's Rapture.

concepts.name: little_sister
concepts.definition: A conditioned child who harvests ADAM in BioShock.

concepts.name: would_you_kindly
concepts.definition: BioShock's mind-control trigger phrase.

concepts.name: portal
concepts.definition: A 2007 puzzle game (Valve) with the antagonist AI GLaDOS; source of 'the cake is a lie'.

concepts.name: glados
concepts.definition: The passive-aggressive antagonist AI of Valve's Portal.

concepts.name: aperture
concepts.definition: Aperture Science, the fictional research company of Portal.

concepts.name: half_life
concepts.definition: Valve's landmark first-person game series, a canon of gaming referents.
